questions.question: Why is the area to the left of a school bus especially dangerous for students?

options.text: Sun reflection makes it hard to see the left side.
Other vehicles drive past on the left side.
The left side of any bus is hard to see.
There is no door on the left side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Other vehicles drive past on the left side.
questions.explanation: All sides of a school bus have danger zones. The left side is most dangerous because passing vehicles are there.

questions.question: School buses:

options.text: Never have ABS.
Only have ABS if the bus carries children under 10 years old.
May have ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have ABS.
questions.explanation: School buses made after 1998 or 1999 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS). Many older buses have ABS as well.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to do which of these?

options.text: Alley dock.
Parallel park to your right.
Parallel park to your left.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: During the driving skills test, after passing under an overpass, you may be asked to remember:

options.text: The posted clearance height.
The posted weight limit.
The width of the opening.
If there was a shoulder near the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The posted clearance height.
questions.explanation: If you drive under an overpass during the road test, the examiner may ask you to recall the posted height or clearance of the overpass.

questions.question: If a school bus gets stuck on railroad tracks:

options.text: Students should stay on the bus.
Students should leave and stay near the bus.
Students should leave and move far away from the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students should leave and move far away from the bus.
questions.explanation: If a school bus gets stuck on railroad tracks, the driver must evacuate everyone immediately. If a train hits the bus, students should move far away at an angle to avoid flying debris.

questions.question: The overhead rearview mirror is located:

options.text: On the outside left of the bus.
On the outside right of the bus.
Above the windshield inside the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield inside the bus.
questions.explanation: The overhead rearview mirror in a school bus is mounted above the windshield on the driver's side.

questions.question: Loading and unloading a bus:

options.text: Can be dangerous for passengers.
Does not need to be supervised.
Should be done while refueling.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be dangerous for passengers.
questions.explanation: More students are killed during loading and unloading of school buses than while riding them. Drivers must follow proper safety procedures during these times.

questions.question: An outside convex mirror is properly adjusted if the driver can see:

options.text: At least one lane of traffic and the entire side of the bus.
The front bumper.
The top of the bus.
The front windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least one lane of traffic and the entire side of the bus.
questions.explanation: The outside side convex mirrors should be positioned so the driver can see the ground where the rear tires touch, both sides of the bus up to the mirrors, and at least one traffic lane on each side.

questions.question: Students loading and unloading a bus:

options.text: Is simple and does not need to be supervised.
Can be dangerous and should be supervised.
May be done without the bus driver present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be dangerous and should be supervised.
questions.explanation: More students are killed during loading and unloading of school buses than while riding them. This process must always be supervised and should never happen without the driver present.

questions.question: Backing a school bus is:

options.text: Strongly encouraged.
Strongly discouraged.
Only to be done in the morning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strongly discouraged.
questions.explanation: Backing a school bus should be avoided whenever possible. Only back up if there is no safe alternative. Always follow proper safety procedures when backing.

questions.question: When checking the fifth wheel during a pre-trip inspection, you should:

options.text: Make sure there is a gap between the kingpin and the locking jaws.
Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
Make sure the locking jaws are loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: Look into the fifth wheel gap and check that the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.

questions.question: Student safety is best maintained by:

options.text: Keeping the students on the bus.
Letting some students evacuate the bus while others stay on.
Letting students evacuate the bus.
Creating panic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeping the students on the bus.
questions.explanation: In most emergency situations, students are safest and easiest to control when they stay on the bus.

questions.question: As students exit the bus, the driver should watch to ensure that:

options.text: They are leaving in pairs.
They do not get caught on the handrail or door.
They do not talk while exiting the bus.
They all have shoes on.

questions.correctAnswerText: They do not get caught on the handrail or door.
questions.explanation: Watch students as they exit to make sure they do not get caught in the door or handrails. Also make sure they move a safe distance away from the bus after exiting.

questions.question: If your bus has a roof-mounted strobe light, use it:

options.text: When visibility is poor.
All the time.
Only at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: When visibility is poor.
questions.explanation: Use the roof-mounted strobe light when weather or other conditions make it hard to see.

questions.question: If a student drops an item while approaching the bus, the student should:

options.text: Stop and pick up the object.
Have another student pick up the object.
Ask the driver to pick up the object.
Just leave the item alone and walk away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask the driver to pick up the object.
questions.explanation: Students should not pick up dropped items because the driver might not see them. Instead, the student should move away from the bus, get the driver's attention, and ask the driver to retrieve the item.

questions.question: If your bus has a manual transmission, you should never ____ while crossing railroad tracks.

options.text: Change gears
Use the brakes
Look both ways
Listen to flaggers

questions.correctAnswerText: Change gears
questions.explanation: Before crossing railroad tracks, check for approaching trains from all directions. Never shift gears while crossing the tracks.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, lug nuts must be all of the following, except:

options.text: Free of cracks.
Free of distortions.
Loose.
Free of rust.

questions.correctAnswerText: Loose.
questions.explanation: Lug nuts must be present and tight. They must be free of cracks, distortions, and rust. Check all bolt holes for cracks and distortions.

questions.question: During the basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Swerve to avoid a hazard.
Parallel park.
Drive straight into a parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parallel park.
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset backing, parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: When exiting your vehicle, you:

options.text: Must maintain four points of contact with the vehicle.
May turn to face the road before your exit is complete.
Must be facing away from the vehicle.
Must be facing the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be facing the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Face the vehicle as you exit. Keep three points of contact with the vehicle at all times. For a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly can result in automatic failure of the test.

questions.question: A properly adjusted flat mirror should allow the driver to see:

options.text: The rear tires touching the ground.
The front tires touching the ground.
Only the roadway and no parts of the bus.
The front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rear tires touching the ground.
questions.explanation: A properly adjusted flat mirror lets the driver see 200 feet behind the bus, where each rear tire touches the ground, and the sides of the bus.
